flags.description: Post-stream clipper (services/clip/clipper.py): ranked candidates, 3 vertical variants, captions, validation. Off until used on a real stream.
flags.label: Clip maker
flags.summary: Makes ranked, ready-to-post clips from a stream after it ends.

flags.description: Live clip markers (F6): the event core writes a marker (source chat) on a 'clip it' message or a chat-speed spike, and (source audio) on an audio peak. Thresholds from data/clip/ranking.json and data/clip/live-markers.json (proposed). Read live; a marker failure never affects the stream. Off until used on a real stream.
flags.label: Live clip markers
flags.summary: Marks big moments during the stream so they are easy to find later.

flags.description: Layer effects (D224): rounded corners on the framed game and the keyed call-to-action videos. Applied when the alpha project is built (--rebuild-alpha). The blurred game backdrop behind every layer (H and V) no longer needs this flag (D331, user request). Off until used on a real stream.
flags.label: Layer effects
flags.summary: Rounded corners on the framed game and call-to-action videos.

flags.description: Live clipping (D226): while streaming, a background worker reads the game picture once a second (GPU OCR when available), spots kill streaks (Triple Kill and up) and saves the replay buffer (H and V) before the streamer's death. Saves are listed for review after the stream; nothing is posted. Switches live: the worker re-reads this flag every 5 s. Off until used on a real stream.
flags.label: Live kill clips
flags.summary: Saves your kill streaks from the replay buffer while you stream.

flags.description: Mouse editing on the preview (P5, D230): click a layer in the H or V preview to select it, drag to move it, drag a corner to resize it (aspect kept; Shift = free), drag the middle of an edge to stretch that side, drag the diamond above the top edge to turn it (Shift = 15 degree steps), Alt + drag an edge to crop that side, snapping to the canvas edges and centre and to the other layers' edges and centres with a guide line (D272; Alt = no snap). The release saves the placement like an inspector edit. Arrow keys on the control page move the selected layer 1 px (Shift 10 px), not while live (D254). Never while live: a press then selects nothing (live-lock, D233). On by default since 2026-11-10 (D330: the user asked for resize and crop on the preview). Switches live: the studio UI server passes it to the host within a second; off ignores the mouse at once.
flags.label: Mouse editing on preview
flags.summary: Select, move, resize, turn and crop layers with the mouse.

flags.description: Advanced effect list (D260, D290): shows the plain, ordered list of a layer's effects under the Look panel in the studio window (add, remove, reorder, tune). The Look panel itself needs no flag. Apply sends the whole list to the host, saves it into the project and can be undone, offline or live. Off by default.
flags.label: Effect list
flags.summary: Shows a layer's effects as an ordered list you can edit.

flags.description: Track routing in the mixer (D273): each sound in the studio window's mixer shows a button per project audio track (track 1 is what the stream and recording hear); click to send the sound to that track or take it out. Saved into the project, offline or live. A sound on no track is listed too, so it can be put back; a layer sound with no project audio entry cannot be routed.
flags.label: Mixer track routing
flags.summary: Choose which audio track each sound goes to.

flags.description: Scene transitions (D239): scene switches fade like Meld, per canvas, using the project's transition (imported from the Meld session: H 2006 ms, V 1000 ms fades). Off: every switch is a cut. Switches live: the studio UI server applies it within a second.
flags.label: Scene transitions
flags.summary: Fades between scenes like Meld instead of cutting.

flags.description: Stream settings in the studio (D327, OS1/OS2/TR1): Settings > Stream (canvas mode, frame rate, output resolution, hardware encoder, video bitrate for the main and portrait canvas, quality preset, audio bitrate) and the streaming outputs list (add, edit, delete; delete asks first), plus Settings > Transitions (type, easing curve and duration per canvas; the portrait canvas can mirror the main canvas; Force complete transition). Values are checked against data/platforms; a value over a platform's stated limit is refused with that limit. Outputs bind to shared encoder rungs (sinks never own encoders). The output graph is built from these settings at the next live start (Ujwalam.cmd --live). Off: the live start uses data/outputs/alpha-live.json as before.
flags.label: Stream settings
flags.summary: Edit canvas, bitrate, encoder and outputs in the studio.

flags.description: Outputs panel in the studio window (D327, OS3): every stream output with an on/off switch, + to add one, and a Virtual Camera row. Offline the switch chooses which outputs Start stream starts; while live it starts or stops only that output at once. Off: Start stream starts every output as before.
flags.label: Outputs panel
flags.summary: Switch each stream output on or off in the studio window.

flags.description: Settings > Integrations (D327, IN1): Streamer.bot and Speaker.bot address and port, a Test button (a plain TCP connect, nothing is sent; Ujwalam stays read-only towards Streamer.bot) and their status, and "Allow remote connections" for the local API: off by default; when on (from the next start) the event core also listens on this PC's private LAN address only (never 0.0.0.0 or a public address), answers only devices on the same local network that present the pairing token, and lets them only ask for actions.
flags.label: Bot connections
flags.summary: Address and test for Streamer.bot and Speaker.bot, and remote access.

flags.description: Scene and layer structure edits (D240): the control page adds and removes scenes and layers (a copy of an existing layer, a colour, a text, a project device or overlay) and saves them into the project file. Refused while live.
flags.label: Scene and layer editing
flags.summary: Add and remove scenes and layers from the control page.

flags.description: Live audience counters (D250): the Twitch/Kick follower and YouTube subscriber counts on the layouts come from Streamer.bot global variables (read-only, every minute; names in data/counters.json) that your own Streamer.bot action keeps up to date; a live follow adds 1 at once. Off: the counter pages show nothing. Switches live.
flags.label: Live counters
flags.summary: Shows follower and subscriber counts on the layouts.

flags.description: Reel transitions (RP1, plan 2026-11-12-reel-polish-music-learning): the join between the pieces of a short, montage, match reel or impact-play reel uses the kind chosen in Settings > Clips (Cut, or Cross fade 150-500 ms; data/clip/transitions.json). A cross fade overlaps each join, so the reel gets that much shorter. A reel with burned-in captions keeps the hard cut. Off: every join is a hard cut with a short sound fade, as before.
flags.label: Reel transitions
flags.summary: Joins reel pieces with a short cross fade instead of a hard cut.

flags.description: Reel start frame (RP6, D366): every montage, match reel, impact-play reel and live clip opens on one edited frame (1/60 s) that acts as its cover: the reel's strongest moment, a short title from its own facts (medal, kills, result, mode) and the brand from the local profile (data/clip/thumbnail.json). Made on this PC with ffmpeg and the bundled fonts. Also kept as thumbnail.png in the reel's folder; posting uses the first frame as the cover. Off: reels open on their first piece as before.
flags.label: Reel start frame
flags.summary: Opens every reel on one edited cover frame with a title.

flags.description: Reel title card (RP4, D362): right after the teaser of a reel (else at its start) the streamer title from the local profile fades in and out over a blurred, darkened copy of the reel, about 1.6 s (data/clip/title.json). Made on this PC with ffmpeg and the bundled fonts. No title without a brand in the profile. Off: reels play without it.
flags.label: Reel title card
flags.summary: Fades your stream title in over a blurred copy of the reel.

flags.description: Reel music beds (RP3, D363, D370): a calm lofi bed under the start of a reel (ending with the title card, or after 3 s) and its last 4 s, made on this PC in plain Python (no AI model, no download, no licence limits), different per reel, about -20 dB and ducked by the game sound so speech stays on top (data/clip/music.json). Off: reels keep only their own sound.
flags.label: Reel music
flags.summary: Adds a calm made-here music bed to the start and end of reels.

flags.description: Growth data (AN1, D371): read your own YouTube numbers (views, watch time, average viewed %, likes, shares, subscribers gained) for the videos Ujwalam posted into a local file on this PC (analytics.db in the app data). Read only: nothing is posted or changed. YouTube sign-in then also asks for the read-only statistics permission; the Google app needs the YouTube Analytics API enabled and that permission added (setup notes: docs/plan/2026-11-12-growth-setup-notes.md). Off: nothing is read.
flags.label: Growth numbers
flags.summary: Reads your own YouTube view and subscriber numbers into a file on this PC.

flags.description: Self-learning within limits (RP5 / AN2, D364, D373): once a week Ujwalam compares the 24 hour and 7 day numbers (flag growth) of the videos it posted and moves the mix of reel kinds and edit choices (transition, title card, music bed, montage length) toward what scored better, with Thompson sampling. Limits in data/clip/learning-mix.json: every choice keeps at least 10 %, a share moves at most 15 points a week; kill rules, detector weights, privacy, posting targets and feature flags never change (a choice is only switched off for some reels, never on). Each change is logged with its numbers in the app data (learning/mix-log.jsonl) and can be undone with one call. With fewer than 8 videos with numbers nothing changes. Off: reels and posts are made exactly as before.
flags.label: Self-learning
flags.summary: Shifts the mix of reel styles toward what gets more views, within limits.

flags.description: Chat-driven effects and event-driven animated layers (example; off until used on a real stream).
flags.label: Chat effects
flags.summary: Lets chat events trigger effects and animated layers.

flags.description: Export-only posting (P16a): review packages of validated clips (video, cover, text) on the Posts view. Nothing is uploaded.
flags.label: Posts window
flags.summary: Prepares clips with cover and text for you to post. Nothing is uploaded.

flags.description: Auto-post approved rules (F7, opt-in): after a stream, `node services/posting/cli.mjs auto --run` marks drafts that match a rule in data/posting/auto-post-rules.json as approved and, only if that file also sets autoUpload, uploads them to YouTube as private. Needs the posting flag. Refuses while any output is live or starting. Off until used; the rules list ships empty.
flags.label: Auto-post
flags.summary: Uploads approved clips to YouTube as private after a stream.

flags.description: Scheduled posting (D310 proposed): each clip the auto-post chain queues goes up to YouTube as private with a publish time, so YouTube makes it public later. The time is 6 hours after the last post already scheduled on the channel (read from YouTube, needs the extra read permission: sign in again after switching this on) or after the last time Ujwalam already gave out, and at least 1 hour from now (data/posting/schedule.json). Times are kept, so a retry never moves a clip. Nothing uploads while live. Needs the posting and auto-post flags. Off: uploads stay private with no publish time.
flags.label: Scheduled posting
flags.summary: Gives each uploaded clip a publish time so YouTube makes it public later.

flags.description: Bot manager (BM1, D193): the Bots card starts, shows and stops the user's installed Streamer.bot and Speaker.bot; only bots Ujwalam started are stopped, also when the studio stops.
flags.label: Bot manager
flags.summary: Starts and stops your Streamer.bot and Speaker.bot from the studio.

flags.description: Test broadcast banner (BM3, D196): a short on-screen note on H and V at stream start and every 15 minutes, telling viewers this is a test of new streaming software. Switches live: the page polls the overlay server every 5 s; off hides it at once.
flags.label: Test broadcast banner
flags.summary: Shows viewers a note that this is a test of new software.

flags.description: Face AI for a camera layer (D295 proposed): background removal / blur / replacement (personMask), a camera that follows the face (autoFrame) and pictures pinned to the face (faceSticker). A local worker runs small ONNX models (data/models/face-ai.json) on the GPU through DirectML and hands masks and face points to the host. Off: the worker unloads its models and these effects show the plain camera. Uses GPU memory and time next to the encoder: measured, not yet approved for live use. Switches live: the worker re-reads this flag every 5 s.
flags.label: Face AI
flags.summary: Background removal, face-following camera and face stickers.

flags.description: Ready to go live? (D299 proposed): a pre-stream check on the control page (stream keys present and the server address scheme, disk space, other streaming apps, Streamer.bot and Speaker.bot, host and outputs, last loopback test, clip maker, audio sources, NVIDIA GPU; thresholds in data/live/readiness.json). Starting the stream runs the check first; a failed item stops the start and lists the problems with a "Go live anyway" button, which is logged as an override. Warnings never block. Off: Start stream goes live at once.
flags.label: Ready to go live check
flags.summary: Checks keys, disk, bots and GPU before the stream starts.

flags.description: Stream recovery after a host crash (D303 proposed): when the studio's video engine (the libobs host) crashes while you are live, Ujwalam restarts it, reloads your scenes and starts again exactly the streams that were live (YouTube H, YouTube V, Twitch, Kick), on the strength of your Start stream click for this session. Never a stream that was not live, never after Stop or End all, never after Ujwalam itself was restarted, at most 2 times in 10 minutes and only when the host is back within 90 s (data/live/recovery.json); then the streams stay off and the control page says why. The recording always restarts into a new file. Off: streams are not restarted (start them by hand). Read at each crash, so it switches live.
flags.label: Stream recovery
flags.summary: Restarts your streams if the video engine crashes while you are live.

flags.description: Host watchdog (D374 proposed): the launcher asks the studio's video engine (the libobs host) every 5 s whether it still runs and still makes video frames. When it has not answered for 30 s, or has made no video frame for 30 s (a frozen GPU, for example after a graphics driver reset), Ujwalam stops it and restarts it the same way as after a crash: the scenes are loaded again, the recording restarts in a new file, and streams come back only when Stream recovery is on and its rules allow it (this switch never starts a stream by itself). At most 3 restarts in 5 minutes, then Ujwalam stops. Each incident shows once in the task bar, with the cause when Windows logged a graphics driver reset. Limits in data/live/host-watch.json. Off: a frozen engine is only written to the log; restart Ujwalam by hand. Read at each check, so it switches live.
flags.label: Host watchdog
flags.summary: Restarts the video engine by itself if it freezes or stops answering.

flags.description: Live test kit (D305 proposed): the studio window and the control page show plain-words alerts (a sound source that stopped, a stream restarted or not after a host crash), remind you for the first minutes after going live to start your own Streamer.bot action (data/live/test-kit.json: it posts the feedback question and has Speaker.bot read the announcement), and when the stream ends the viewers' replies are collected read-only into feedback/YYYY-MM-DD-stream-feedback.md (local only). Ujwalam never posts in chat, never speaks and never triggers a Streamer.bot action. Switches live.
flags.label: Live test kit
flags.summary: Plain-words alerts while live and viewer replies collected after.

flags.description: Payoff-first hook (ED1, D352): every kill montage, match reel, impact-play reel and live clip opens on its strongest moment (the best kill or the multi-kill) within the first 3 seconds, then plays in order. A montage moves the piece with that moment to the front; a match reel, impact-play reel or live clip gets a short teaser of it (1-3 s, Settings > Clips) before the reel from its start. The reel stays within its maximum length, teaser included; it never opens on a death; each part of a split reel gets its own opening from its own content. Settings > Clips has Open with the best moment and the teaser length for each reel type. A hook score (kill, multi-kill, medal and motion in the first 3 s) is saved with every reel either way. Off: reels open as before.
flags.label: Reel hook
flags.summary: Opens every reel on its strongest moment within the first 3 seconds.

flags.description: Story montages (RP2, D361, user 2026-11-12): each kill montage opens with a fast cut of the strongest kills (about 4 s), then tells one match in order with the dead time cut; only when that match has too few kills do the best kills of other matches follow it. The match's own result screen ends the montage only when it was won or top 3 and nothing from another match follows; no other result screen is ever shown. Kills already in the stream's live clips are left out when the montage can be made without them, and no kill is used in two montages. The title card goes between the fast cut and the story (RP4, later). Off: montages as before (best streaks first, matches mixed). Victory and summary screens are left out of montages either way.
flags.label: Montage story
flags.summary: Builds each kill montage as a fast best-of intro, then one match in order.

flags.description: Burned-in captions (ED2, D353): the clip maker transcribes what was said live with the local speech to text and burns captions into kill montages, match reels, impact-play reels and live clips, inside the vertical safe zone. Only segments the speech to text is confident about are shown; text is kept in the script it was spoken in. Malayalam text is not burned yet (no bundled caption font covers Malayalam) but stays in the transcript. Each reel keeps its transcript next to it (transcript.json); after you edit it, clipper.py recaption renders the reel again. Needs the local speech-to-text model. Off: no captions.
flags.label: Reel captions
flags.summary: Burns what was said into reels as captions.

flags.description: Impact-play reels (D326, user feedback 2026-11-10): when the clip maker makes the kill montages and match reels of a recording, it also cuts one separate reel per match whose IMPACT PLAY screen shows your name, from the MVP animation through the impact-play camera to the results page (rules in data/games/<game>/match-reels.json impactPlay). Saved to your clips folder as impact-play files; auto-post does not pick them up yet. Off: no impact-play reel is made.
flags.label: Impact-play reels
flags.summary: Cuts a separate reel of each match where you got the impact play.

flags.description: Scene builder from a reference (SB1-SB5, D339, D341, D345, D347): reads a local reference image or video (a video is sampled to N frames) into data: its palette, type feel, corner radius, glow and shadow use, and where the game, camera, chat, alerts and graphics sit, each with a confidence. Rules only; a local vision model can plug in later through a typed hook, never a paid API. SB3 (D341): builds one NEW namespaced H + V scene from that read, linked to your own capture layers, devices and overlays by reference, with placeholders for unsure or unmatched slots; it shows a dry-run diff first and never changes an existing scene, layer, device or setting. SB4 (D345): makes a studio theme from the same reference (colours, corners, glow and shadow to a theme pack that passes the contrast check), saved as a new custom theme only when you ask. SB5 (D347): iterate. Saves a scene of your project (for example a built scene you then adjusted in the studio) as a scene package, edits a package (move, resize, swap two slots), and makes up to 8 similar variants (seeded, kept inside the canvas and the V safe zone, game never cropped further); none of it changes your project, and a saved package is imported like any other. Today the only way in is the command node services/scene-builder/cli.mjs read|build|import|theme|export|edit|variants. Off: the command refuses.
flags.label: Scene builder
flags.summary: Builds a scene look from a reference image or video.

flags.description: Report button (D199): the control page opens a prefilled GitHub new-issue page in your browser (title, version, OS, flags, counts-only diagnostics). Needs links.issues_url in the local profile. Nothing is sent by Ujwalam; you review and submit in the browser.
flags.label: Report button
flags.summary: Opens a prefilled GitHub issue page in your browser.

flags.description: Review reads (LL3, D340): after a stream, My clips shows a Review reads button when the clip maker queued reads it was not sure of (a VICTORY/DEFEAT banner it could not place as round or match end, a match whose game mode it could not tell, a text read below the game pack's OCR confidence). Each item shows its frame; you confirm or correct it with one click, which saves a label in the local learning store. Optional: nothing waits for it. Off: the button is hidden; reads are still queued in the local store.
flags.label: Review uncertain reads
flags.summary: Lets you confirm or correct what the clip maker was unsure about.

flags.description: Platform sign-in in the studio (D327, PC1-PC3): Settings > Connections signs in to YouTube (Google) or Twitch and fetches the stream key for each output, or takes a pasted stream key and server address (Kick, custom RTMP). Ujwalam writes the keys and sign-in tokens to Windows Credential Manager itself (the same names the studio host reads), shows only the last 4 characters, and Disconnect deletes them. Every change happens on your click; a live output's key is never changed while it streams. Off: keys are set with the credential command as before.
flags.label: Platform sign-in
flags.summary: Sign in to YouTube or Twitch and fetch stream keys in the studio.

flags.description: Service swap while live (LU3, D337): the event core and the studio UI server are reached through fixed ports the launcher owns, so a new version of either can replace the running one without a dropped event, a new port or a logged-out page; a new version that fails its check is stopped and the old one keeps running. Live updates (LU5, LU7, D343): while a stream or recording runs, a service update waits for one Apply now click on the control page, and a host update (the overlay server goes with it) is staged and applied when everything has stopped, or tried at the next start if Ujwalam closes first (a release that fails is never tried again). Stream and recording starts are held while the host is replaced. Live install (LU6, D349): Install-Ujwalam.ps1 run while Ujwalam runs hands the new version to this queue (the same click and stop rules); without the flag it installs next to the running copy for the next start. Read at start: switch it, then restart Ujwalam. Off: the services start as before.
flags.label: Service swap
flags.summary: Replaces a background service with a new version without dropping events.

flags.description: Theme components (D336, T1 of the theme framework): a theme pack may describe its component language as data (button shape and style, tabs, inputs, focus, switch, slider, section headers, cards, lists, chips, layout density, caps and a type scale, raised, sunken and metal-rimmed edges, blueprint and column backdrops). The studio window then draws those variants, and Settings > Appearance shows Preview all components. Studio window only: never touches the stream, the scenes or the outputs. Packs without a components block look the same either way. Switches live: the studio window redraws within a few seconds. Off: every pack draws with the base look.
flags.label: Theme components
flags.summary: Lets themes restyle buttons, tabs, inputs and cards.

flags.description: Game pack tuning from your streams (LL4, D342): after a stream, once its clips are made, a low-priority job reads the labels in the local learning store (your answers in Review reads) and proposes a new game pack version only when it reads held-out streams better than the current pack. The proposal is saved as a local candidate with its score and evidence (status unverified) and never applies itself: you approve it with pack_tune.py approve. Nothing runs while a stream is live and no model is loaded. Off: no tuning runs and no candidate is made or approved.
flags.label: Learn from my streams
flags.summary: Proposes better game settings from your reviewed answers, never applied alone.

flags.description: Instagram Live output (IG1, D351): at the --live start an instagram stream is added to the live plan, fed from the V canvas (9:16) on its own 720x1280 30 fps rung, or on the V rung when that one fits Instagram's limits (data/platforms/instagram.json). Instagram gives a new stream URL and key for every broadcast: paste both in Settings > Connections > Instagram or in the Instagram Live box on the control page (needs platform-connect); they go to Windows Credential Manager only. A key used for a broadcast that ended counts as used, and the readiness check fails until a new one is pasted. Read at the start: a change applies from the next --live start. Off until used on a real stream.
flags.label: Instagram Live
flags.summary: Adds an Instagram Live output from the vertical canvas.
